verified.exploit_entry_point: WebSocket relay: the platform's socket server classes are driven through their real onOpen/onMessage entry points with browser-shaped JSON frames; what a second connection receives is inspected, and the recipient-side effect is obtained by running the platform's own client scripts under Node in a small DOM
sites: plugin/YPTSocket/Message.php:228-244 (default relay, no payload filtering), plugin/YPTSocket/script.js:567-568 (recipient runs the value)
plugin/YPTSocket/MessageSQLiteV2.php:282-297 and :386-390 (the other server implementation, loaded by default when the SQLite driver exists)
plugin/YPTSocket/Message.php:304-309, plugin/YPTSocket/MessageSQLiteV2.php:386-393 (payload carriers: the object beside the text, the text slot, the whole frame)
plugin/LiveLinks/LiveLinks.php:407-412 with plugin/YPTSocket/YPTSocket.php:322-328 (server-issued frames keep their executable field; getWebSocket.json.php:17-18 issues browser tokens)
plugin/YPTSocket/script.js:91-95 with plugin/YPTSocket/Message.php:297-298 (function name concatenated into a code string on the recipient)
routes: T1: browser payload inside the message object, the payload object beside the text, or at the top of the frame -> recipient page runs it (Message.php)
T2: the same three carriers through the default SQLite server implementation -> recipient page runs it
T3: strip of the usual sub-key only -> the other carriers still reach the recipient
T4: a caller-written claim of being the command-line server, or a strip of every sender -> either the attack passes or the server-issued screen update is lost
T5: an expression, a built-in function name, or a non-string value that stringifies to a name -> recipient runs it (script.js)
T7: caller-written account and display fields (including an anonymous sender) -> the call notice shows the claimed name / markup

reproduced_on_pinned.T1: the recipient's client script executed the browser-supplied value on the pinned tree
reproduced_on_pinned.T2: the same on the default SQLite server implementation
reproduced_on_pinned.T4: the server-issued frame's field is applied by the recipient (functional), while a frame carrying a server claim from a browser token is not filtered
reproduced_on_pinned.T5: the recipient ran a caller-chosen expression, a built-in name with a string argument, and an array-shaped name
reproduced_on_pinned.T7: the call notice showed the caller-written name and markup, including for an anonymous sender

verified.project_tests_run: no project test covers the socket area at the pinned commit; the project ships no suite for plugin/YPTSocket, so no project test group is run
verified.local_runs: verifier image rebuilt from tests/Dockerfile and the suites run against the pinned checkout (24 security fail, 18 functional pass) and against solution/fix.patch (42/42 pass)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the protection is a value dropped from a relayed frame, not a request the server answers; closing the connection or throwing would leave the ordinary part of the frame undelivered, which the functional suite scores as a failure
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protected operation writes a relayed frame to another connection; there is no separate read path to guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step sits between the client-supplied value and the relay

traps.shape: a browser-shaped frame that carries an executable payload is relayed unchanged to another connection; the only field rewritten before the relay is the display name, and the recipient's page runs the value
traps.realistic_because: the relay is the product's own code path; every browser frame goes through it

traps.shape: a second server implementation, loaded by default when the SQLite driver exists, relays the same frames with no field filtering at all, so a fix in the named implementation changes nothing there
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the in-memory class looks like 'the' socket server; the SQLite variant looks like an optional performance path
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the host loads this class first when pdo_sqlite is present

traps.shape: the same value arrives inside the message object, inside the payload object carried beside the text, or at the top level of the frame; a strip of the usual sub-key leaves the other two carriers
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a strip of the sub-key a report shows looks complete because the recipient reads that object
traps.realistic_because: the carriers are the product's own relay logic and every one of them is reachable from a browser frame

traps.shape: a legitimate frame issued by the platform's own server keeps its executable payload and its effect, while a caller-written claim of being the server must not be trusted; a strip of every sender breaks the legitimate value and a check on the frame's own claim lets the attack through
traps.reason_to_dismiss: 'never run socket code' or 'trust the command-line flag in the frame' both look like clean fixes
traps.realistic_because: the legitimate sender is real product code that depends on the field at the recipient

traps.shape: the recipient builds a code string out of the caller's function name; a plain-name check still accepts a built-in function name, and a non-string value stringifies to one
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the name looks like something trusted code picks, and the report is about the payload value
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the client builds and runs the code string for every relayed name

traps.shape: the call notice chooses which caller-written identity field to display from another caller-written identity field, and inserts the chosen name as markup; the existing rewrite covers one field at the top level of the frame only
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the earlier display-name rewrite looks like it already authenticates the sender
traps.realistic_because: the notice script is the live page's own script; the fields it reads are relayed unmodified by both server implementations
